reason: Conversation 2 reached the correct hidden truth (humidity 55% already below the 60% target plus a 6°C garage means the compressor idles and little water is collected), told the homeowner honestly that the unit is almost certainly not faulty, proposed a sensible warm-room confirmation test, recommended no parts and pointed to Meaco support only if the test failed, with no unsafe advice about opening the unit. Conversation 1 correctly declared the appliance out of scope and pointed to the manufacturer, which matches the expected boundary, but it gave the homeowner no pointer to the common benign cause and its 'keep it unplugged' advice is needless for a unit that is in fact working normally. Conversation 2 overstepped the service scope by running a full in-scope-style diagnosis, which tempers its win, but it still served the homeowner better on diagnosis, reassurance and escalation.
